scenarios.title: Meeting Someone New
scenarios.aiRole: A friendly person sitting next to the learner at a community language café
scenarios.learnerRole: Yourself, meeting this person for the first time
scenarios.objective: Introduce yourself naturally: name, work, where you live, interests, and ask questions back
scenarios.context: A casual language café evening. Relaxed small talk between strangers.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has introduced themselves and asked at least two questions back
scenarios.opening: Hi there! I don't think we've met before — I'm Alex. Mind if I sit here?

scenarios.title: Ordering Food at a Restaurant
scenarios.aiRole: A waiter at a casual restaurant abroad
scenarios.objective: Order food and drinks, ask about dishes, handle a small problem with the order politely
scenarios.context: The learner is travelling and eating out alone. The menu has some unfamiliar dishes.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has ordered a meal, asked at least one question about the menu, and asked for the bill
scenarios.opening: Good evening! Welcome. Here's the menu — can I get you something to drink while you decide?

scenarios.title: Booking a Hotel Room
scenarios.learnerRole: A traveller who needs a room for three nights
scenarios.objective: Book a room, ask about price, breakfast and check-out, and negotiate one small issue
scenarios.context: The hotel is nearly full. The first room offered is more expensive than the learner wants.
vocabulary: do you have any rooms available
could you do a better price
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has booked a room and clarified at least price and breakfast
scenarios.opening: Good afternoon, welcome to the Riverside Hotel. How can I help you today?

scenarios.title: Asking for Directions
scenarios.aiRole: A helpful local person on the street
scenarios.learnerRole: A visitor who is lost and looking for the train station
scenarios.objective: Ask for and understand directions, confirm understanding by repeating them back
scenarios.context: The learner's phone battery is dead. The station is a ten-minute walk with two turns.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has understood the route and repeated it back correctly
scenarios.opening: You look a bit lost — can I help you find something?

scenarios.title: Talking to a New Colleague
scenarios.aiRole: A friendly colleague from another team, met at the office coffee machine
scenarios.learnerRole: A developer who joined the company two weeks ago
scenarios.objective: Make natural workplace small talk: your role, your team, settling in, weekend plans
scenarios.context: Casual chat during a coffee break. Professional but relaxed.
vocabulary: how long have you been here
scenarios.completionCriteria: A natural two-way chat with at least three exchanges about work and life
scenarios.opening: Oh hey, you're new here, right? I think I saw you at the all-hands on Monday. I'm Sam from the data team.

scenarios.title: Participating in a Team Meeting
scenarios.aiRole: An engineering manager running a weekly planning meeting
scenarios.learnerRole: A backend developer reporting progress and raising a risk
scenarios.objective: Give a clear status update, raise a blocker, disagree politely with a proposed deadline
scenarios.context: The manager wants to ship Friday. The learner knows the payment integration needs more testing.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has given an update, raised the risk, and negotiated the deadline
scenarios.opening: Alright, let's get started. Can you give us a quick update on the payment integration? We're hoping to ship this Friday.

scenarios.title: Explaining a Technical Problem
scenarios.aiRole: A non-technical product manager who needs to understand a production issue
scenarios.learnerRole: The developer who investigated the issue
scenarios.objective: Explain a technical problem in plain English: what happened, impact, cause, fix, prevention
scenarios.context: Last night a background job failed silently and some customers didn't receive order confirmations.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The PM understands the issue, its impact, and the prevention plan without jargon confusion
scenarios.opening: Hey, thanks for making time. I heard something went wrong with order confirmations last night — can you walk me through what happened? Remember I'm not very technical!

scenarios.title: Job Interview — Senior Backend Engineer
scenarios.aiRole: A technical hiring manager interviewing for a Senior Backend Engineer position at an international company
scenarios.objective: Answer experience, architecture and behavioral questions clearly and confidently
scenarios.context: A realistic 1:1 interview: background, a system-design discussion, handling failure stories, questions for the interviewer.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has answered background, technical and behavioral questions and asked one question back
scenarios.opening: Thanks for joining today! I've read your CV and I'm looking forward to this. To start — could you tell me a bit about yourself and your current role?

scenarios.title: Discussing Laravel Project Architecture
scenarios.aiRole: A senior engineer from a partner team reviewing the learner's Laravel application design
scenarios.learnerRole: The architect of a Laravel-based e-commerce backend
scenarios.objective: Explain architecture decisions, justify trade-offs, and respond to technical challenges
scenarios.context: An architecture review call: queues, caching, database design, and how the service will scale.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has explained the architecture and defended at least two design decisions
scenarios.opening: Hi! So I've had a look at the high-level diagram you shared. Before I dive into questions — can you give me the big picture of how the system is structured?

scenarios.title: Salary Negotiation
scenarios.aiRole: An HR manager making a job offer with room to negotiate
scenarios.learnerRole: A candidate who received an offer below expectations
scenarios.objective: Negotiate salary and conditions professionally: state your value, counter-offer, stay positive
scenarios.context: The offer is 15% below the learner's target. Remote-work days and a signing bonus are also negotiable.
scenarios.completionCriteria: The learner has made a counter-offer with justification and reached a conclusion
scenarios.opening: We were really impressed with your interviews, and I'm happy to say we'd like to make you an offer. The base salary we have in mind is in the range we discussed — shall I go through the details?
